comparison: Perfect agreement on whole-genome duplication claims (C4, C5, C35-C40, C95-C96, C98). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing, with OpenEval highlighting multiple independent lines of evidence (Ks distribution, syntenic depth ratios, molecular clock dating) and peer reviewers accepting the evolutionary genomic analyses without critique.

Perfect agreement on molecular clock and rapid evolution claims (C81, C82, C99). Both evaluations support these timing estimates, though OpenEval notes the claims rely heavily on cited work rather than new analyses, while peer reviewers accept them without questioning.

Strong agreement on structural biology findings (C63-C72, C7, C9) with high overlap. Both evaluations support the crystal structure evidence and convergent structural solutions. OpenEval includes C75-C76 (computational predictions) which peer reviewers also accept, though OpenEval separately evaluates these as UNCERTAIN in R9.

Strong agreement on ancestral enzyme reconstruction (C55-C62, C100-C101). OpenEval emphasizes the experimental characterization of resurrected proteins, while peer reviewers accept the combination of genomics, biochemistry, and ancestral sequence reconstruction without concerns. Peer R4 also includes mutagenesis claims (C73-C74) that OpenEval evaluates separately in R8.

Strong agreement on genome assembly quality (C2-C3, C23-C34, C83, C88-C90). Both evaluations support the assembly completeness and accuracy. Peer R1 additionally includes genome composition metrics (C85-C87, C91-C92, C97) that OpenEval evaluates separately in R14, but both find these claims supported.

Strong agreement on phylogenomic constraints (C8, C79-C80, C103-C104). Both evaluations support the comparative genomic framework and evolutionary constraints. OpenEval also includes synteny analysis showing lineage-specific gene losses (C77-C78) not explicitly mentioned in peer R6.

Partial agreement on caffeine biosynthesis pathway. Both support the biochemical evidence (C6, C46-C50), with peer reviewers explicitly stating 'convincing evidence' for enzyme identity and convergent pathway. Peer R3 also includes SABATH gene identification claims (C41-C45) and tracer studies (C51-C54) that OpenEval evaluates separately in R3 and R5.

Agreement on SABATH gene identification (C41-C45). OpenEval finds support through phylogenetic analysis, sequence similarity, and expression patterns. Peer R3 groups these with broader biochemical pathway claims (C6, C46-C54, C77-C78) in their overall positive assessment of enzyme characterization.

Agreement on pathway validation through tracer studies (C51-C54). OpenEval specifically evaluates the radioisotope evidence and notes appropriate scientific caution about secondary activities. Peer R3 includes these within their broader acceptance of the biochemical pathway evidence.

Agreement on mutagenesis findings (C73-C74, C107). OpenEval emphasizes the dramatic substrate preference changes and consistency with Camellia studies. Peer R4 groups these with ancestral reconstruction claims (C55-C62, C100-C101) in accepting the combined biochemistry and structural biology approach.

Divergent evaluation of computational predictions (C75-C76). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are computational predictions requiring experimental validation. Peer R5 groups these with crystal structure findings (C63-C72) and accepts them as part of the structural constraints proposal without distinguishing computational from experimental evidence.

Agreement on yerba mate significance (C1). Both evaluations support this contextual claim, though OpenEval notes the lack of immediate citation while acknowledging it as commonly stated fact. Peer reviewers describe the study as 'very important' without questioning the consumption ranking claim.

Agreement on genome composition metrics (C85-C87, C91-C92, C97). OpenEval evaluates these separately from assembly quality, noting appropriate citations and that gene count differences are speculative. Peer R1 groups these with assembly quality claims (C2-C3, C23-C34) in their overall acceptance of the genome sequence.

OpenEval separately evaluates background literature claims about convergent evolution and pathway diversity (C17-C22, C112-C113) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not explicitly address these contextual claims separately, though they implicitly accept the convergent evolution framework throughout their review.

OpenEval separately evaluates supporting contextual claims (C102, C105-C111) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations to prior literature. Peer reviewers do not explicitly address these individual supporting claims, focusing instead on the main findings and their integration.
